extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/faculty and research administrators at U.S. institutions of higher education preparing DURIP (DoD) instrumentation proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for preparing and submitting Defense University Research Instrumentation Program (DURIP) proposals to DoD tri-service agencies, including allowable costs, proposal content, and submission logistics. Focused on 12-month instrumentation acquisition awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Criterion — Impact on DoD-funded research and research capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The impact of your proposed equipment or instrumentation on research DoD funds, or plans to fund, and/or the likelihood your proposed equipment or instrumentation will enhance current research capabilities or establish new research capabilities relevant to DoD areas of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should clearly explain how the equipment will enhance or create research capabilities of relevance to DoD, with specific examples. Relevance to existing DoD-funded work can make this easier to demonstrate, but past/current DoD support is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Criterion — Importance and priority to DoD missions
rubrics_metrics.description: The importance and priority to DoD missions of research your proposed equipment or instrumentation will support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address specific DoD mission priorities and show alignment with program officer research interests. Route your proposal to a single core technical program officer (PO) whose interests best match and discuss how the equipment supports DoD priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Criterion — Potential to enhance education of future scientists and engineers
rubrics_metrics.description: The potential your proposed equipment or instrumentation offers to enhance your institution’s ability to educate future scientists and engineers through research conducted with the proposed equipment in disciplines important to DoD missions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe research-based training opportunities (undergrad/grad exposure to state-of-the-art instrumentation). Emphasize research education rather than general classroom instruction; DURIP is not an education program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Eligible institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: DURIP is open to all not-for-profit U.S. institutions of higher education with degree-granting programs in STEM fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No past, current, or pending DoD support required and no citizenship requirements for personnel. Confirm institutional eligibility before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award characteristics — Duration and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: 12-month awards for acquisition of basic research equipment/instrumentation; DURIP is not a research award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds are meant for acquiring instrumentation to build research capacity and workforce training opportunities; proposals should be for acquisition (or design/manufacture by vendor) rather than supporting research effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award characteristics — Funding floor and ceiling
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum award floor is $50,000 and the program ceiling is $3,000,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no preferred dollar amount. Proposals should justify the requested amount relative to equipment cost and program impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost allowability — Indirect/overhead and salaries
rubrics_metrics.description: DURIP does not cover overhead/indirect costs. Faculty and student salary/effort are not allowed costs under DURIP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universities should plan to absorb indirect costs; ensure salary requests are avoided. Technician labor in bona fide university technician status may be allowable (see technician eligibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost allowability — Vendor design and subcontract policy
rubrics_metrics.description: DURIP does not support subcontracts in general, but a vendor can be paid for design and paid to build/integrate instrumentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may include vendor-paid design/fabrication/integration costs in vendor quotes. Confirm with PO if complex arrangements are planned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vendor quotes required and cost reasonableness
rubrics_metrics.description: Vendor quotes are required to be included as part of the application package to demonstrate cost reasonableness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes should reflect expected discounts to academic clients if provided. Exact vendor identification is not strictly required, but quotes are required; include quotations to show cost reasonableness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installation, training, and calibration costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Installation, initial training, and calibration should be included in vendor quotes and are allowable as part of the equipment acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial vendor training may be funded with limits (e.g., DoD may not pay for entire lab travel to vendor offsite training; PI training or onsite vendor training typically allowable). Extended maintenance and extended warranties are not covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance, warranties, spare parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Extended maintenance fees and extended warranties are not allowable DURIP costs; spare parts/maintenance typically not covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for ongoing maintenance costs to be covered by the institution. DURIP may fund initial setup/validation but not long-term maintenance or multi-year warranties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and remodeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction is not allowable under DURIP; remodeling is generally not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If installation costs include non-allowable construction, those costs should be excluded. Non-construction installation activities by vendors (e.g., equipment siting, hookups) that are not construction may be allowable if documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and expenditure expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Goal is to have DURIP funds 100% expended within 12-18 months from award; instruments typically should be received within the 12-month project period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occasionally a no-cost extension may be granted with sufficient justification. Contact the PO/awarding office for questions about timing and invoicing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software licenses and custom software
rubrics_metrics.description: Software licenses are allowed for the 12-month duration of DURIP but not beyond that timeframe. Custom software may be procured via a contract to a company; faculty/student salary for software development is not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include software license duration limits in budget justification. Subcontracts are generally not supported, but vendor contracts to provide custom software can be considered—discuss with PO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel payment eligibility (technicians vs faculty/students)
rubrics_metrics.description: DURIP funds can pay university technicians or engineers in technician status; faculty and students are not eligible to be paid with DURIP funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that any labor charged to DURIP is for individuals in allowable technician classifications. Research associates may not qualify—confirm status with awarding office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to demonstrate relevance and route to PO
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevance to the DoD mission is a critical component of a competitive proposal; proposers are encouraged to identify and connect with a best-fit core technical program officer (PO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussions with PO help craft language and 'buzz words' to show relevance. The name of the relevant PO must be placed in block 4b of the SF-424 cover page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal content depth — describing the research enabled
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should be explained at a level that thoroughly and completely addresses the evaluation criteria; results/publications are not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the research use cases, how equipment enables DoD-relevant research, and the educational/training aspects. High-level statements are insufficient; provide enough detail to address the three evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of support are allowed but are not part of the required pieces nor part of the evaluation criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may include letters as supplemental material but do not rely on them as evaluative criteria—focus narrative on the stated evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple equipment items and systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple pieces of equipment, or a system/network of equipment, may be proposed in a single DURIP proposal if they together enable a research capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposing systems/networks, justify why all components are necessary. For multi-institution systems you may submit one proposal from a lead institution or separate proposals per institution—administrative costs for cross-institution management are not covered by DURIP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-agency submission and routing
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals can be submitted to more than one funding agency (AFOSR, ARO, ONR); if submitting to multiple agencies, indicate this on the SF-424 cover page and identify a best-fit PO at each agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each agency reviews and prioritizes its own proposals; AFOSR compiles recommendations across agencies and OSD provides final review. Contact each agency PO when proposing cross-service relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-PI award structure and award vesting
rubrics_metrics.description: DURIPs are single-PI awards that award to and vest with the proposing institution; DURIP awards do not include co-PIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List collaborators/key personnel appropriately (co-investigators or key personnel) but understand the award vests with the institution and the PI/co-PI structure differs from multi-PI grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation process and panels
rubrics_metrics.description: At minimum, the core technical program officer evaluates proposals. If conflicts exist, review may be by proxy or panel. Agency recommendations are compiled and OSD reviews/approves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that final funding depends on agency budgets and priorities; ‘cut line’ is determined by available funds and proposal priorities in a given year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cut line and success rate
rubrics_metrics.description: The cut line refers to the budget available each competition year; if below the cut line a proposal may be recommended but unfunded due to budget limits. Typical success rates are broadly on the order of one-quarter to one-third of proposals (variable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect variability year-to-year and dependence on the cost of selected proposals and congressional add-ons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-proposal contact and white papers
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers or short idea statements are not required but may be requested/preferred by individual POs during pre-proposal discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use preproposal contact (deadline noted in FOA) to get PO feedback; the preproposal inquiry deadline applies to contact with POs and DURIP admin offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget presentation and multi-option budgets
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes and detailed budgets are required to gauge cost reasonableness. Including multiple budget options (minimum/mid-range/optimal) is allowable and may be useful—discuss preferences with PO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be as detailed as possible about requested costs; DURIP does not expect proposers to be held to a vendor after award but needs enough detail to judge cost reasonableness.

rubrics_metrics.name: HPC and use of existing DoD facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for high-performance computing (HPC) instrumentation must strongly justify why existing DoD facilities cannot be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If DoD already has facilities that meet needs, proposals for HPC will need a compelling explanation why DURIP acquisition is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferability of award
rubrics_metrics.description: DURIP awards vest with the institution, but transfer to a new institution upon PI job change is handled case-by-case by the awarding office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the awarding office early if PI relocation is anticipated; transferability depends on awarding office policies and discussions among institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference factors (faculty status, student level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty status (junior vs senior) is not considered in evaluation. There is no stated preference for undergrad vs grad student education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on demonstrating educational/research impact rather than faculty seniority or student level. Emphasize research training opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: CV formatting and application document formats
rubrics_metrics.description: AFOSR, ARO, and ONR do not have formatting requirements for CVs (short vitae).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short vitae may follow typical agency/NSF style; follow any FOA-specified page limits or submission instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative costs for multi-institution proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: If one proposal covers multiple universities, DURIP will not pay administrative costs associated with managing the DURIP across the network of institutions (no overhead/indirect costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan institutional administrative support outside of DURIP funds, and be explicit in narrative how management will be handled without charging overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable travel costs
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD would not typically pay for travel to identify and validate equipment to purchase; travel may be allowable in limited circumstances (e.g., PI training) but proposers should expect equipment to be identified before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include travel only when justified and allowable; vendor validation/installation is expected and typically part of vendor services.
